back: Staff grouped by the work they do (production, marketing, finance, HR); simple and specialist but may be slow across departments.
Staff report to a functional manager and a project manager; flexible and good for projects but may cause conflict.
Divisions for product groups, each with its own functions; gives focus but duplicates costs.
Units for regions or countries; local knowledge and quick local decisions but duplication and weaker central control.
Tall: many levels, narrow spans, close supervision, slow communication. Flat: few levels, wide spans, faster communication, more delegation.
Removing levels of management from the hierarchy; widens spans, cuts cost, speeds communication, may overload managers.
Growth, new strategy or products, technology, cost reduction, competition and poor performance.
ZIMSEC uses divisional for structures divided by product or region; Cambridge names product-based and geographic separately.
Match the structure to size, product range, locations and objectives; review it as the business changes.
